issues.issue: The clause makes this Confirmation prevail over the June 15, 2005 Master Repurchase Agreement on "any inconsistency", which is the hinge for whether the Confirmation's Termination Value and Buyer's Margin Amount terms displace Paragraph 4's margin machinery. Whether those terms are a permitted "modification" or an overriding "inconsistency" needs construction.

The all-caps disclosure treats Termination Value as applying to a voluntary early termination priced "as if BCI was the non-defaulting party", while the operative "Termination Value" definition confines it to early termination resulting from an Event of Default. The two statements of the same term diverge.
"Private Label MBS (AAA)" identifies the Purchased Securities only by asset class and rating. Its content depends wholly on the separate CUSIP line.

The entry names Barclays Capital Inc. and Thornburg Mortgage Inc. under a single "Buyer" heading, with no label attaching Thornburg to the Seller role. On its face the line does not say which party is which.

The roll date is "the 16th day of the next succeeding month following the Subsequent Transaction", which does not say whether the month runs from the preceding Repurchase Date or from the new Transaction's own Purchase Date. The reference point is unstated.
The fixed leg is stated as a rate "p.a., fixed, adjusted", and nothing says what "adjusted" means or by reference to what. The word changes the rate actually payable.
The "Buyers Margin Percentage" line is left blank, so the Confirmation states no percentage at all. A term expressed as a heading with no value cannot be applied as written.

The blank leaves the "Buyer's Margin Amount" clause, which computes margin by "application of the Buyer's Margin Percentage to the Repurchase Price", without an input. The Confirmation cannot be operated as a whole on its own terms.
"Notwithstanding the foregoing" has no identified antecedent, leaving unclear which preceding terms the Buyer's termination right overrides. The rest of the mechanic is specific.
The Initial Transaction is defined by reference to "the first Repurchase Date specified below", but the Repurchase Date item appears above this entry. The cross-reference points the wrong way.
Replacement securities need only be "acceptable to Buyer, in Buyer's discretion", and no deadline is fixed for Seller's substitution obligation. Both the standard and the timing are left open.

This clause requires substitution on every Downgrade Event, while the "Substitutions; Eligible Securities for Substitution" clause caps substitutions at twice a month and subjects further ones to Buyer's absolute discretion. The two cannot both operate as written.

"Termination Value" turns on what a hypothetical "Dealer of recognized standing" "would be willing to pay" and on what is "necessary to compensate the non-defaulting party fairly", all determined "in good faith". Each standard is open-textured and controls the amount.

The definition measures Termination Value only for early termination "as a result of the occurrence of an Event of Default", yet the "Buyer's Margin Amount" clause requires a Termination Value "as of any date" with no default. The two must be reconciled by construction.

Termination Value is payable "in addition to any other amounts owing ... pursuant to the provisions of Paragraph 11 of the Agreement", which raises double-recovery. It must be read against the Termination Value definition's carve-out of Paragraph 11 amounts.
"As determined as if Buyer were the non-defaulting party" requires valuation on a counterfactual without saying what else is assumed. The content of the margin add-on is left unfixed.

The clause requires a Termination Value "as of any date", but the "Termination Value" definition supplies a figure only on early termination for an Event of Default. What the definition yields on an ordinary margin day must be construed.
The formula applies "the Buyer's Margin Percentage", but the "Buyers Margin Percentage" line in this same Confirmation is left blank. The clause has no input for limb (i).

The clause supplements Paragraph 4 of the Agreement by splitting Margin Deficits and Excesses into two independently calculated groups of Transactions. Whether margin may be aggregated across those groups, as Paragraph 4 would otherwise contemplate, is left to construction.

The clause appoints Barclays to determine the Termination Value used in its own margin calls without stating any standard in the clause itself. What constrains that self-interested determination must come from elsewhere.

The "Termination Value" definition frames the figure as compensation of "the non-defaulting party", while this clause makes Barclays Calculation Agent for margin purposes when neither party has defaulted. The provisions must be read together to know what is measured.

The clause opens by making substitution subject to "Buyer's sole and absolute discretion" yet then imposes objective conditions and allows two substitutions per month. Whether Seller has a qualified right to substitute twice monthly or needs Buyer's consent each time is genuinely uncertain.

The "Credit Rating" clause obliges Seller to substitute on every Downgrade Event, while this clause caps substitutions at twice monthly and makes further ones discretionary. The two pull against each other.

The paragraph requests signature and return within three Business Days, then provides that failure to respond "shall not affect the validity or enforceability of the Transactions as against you". Whether an unsigned Confirmation binds, and on whose terms, is left open by the same sentence.
